text:
Izzy Wong: Morning all! Happy first week :) Quick setup issues: (1) Monitor arrived but VESA holes don't line up with the arm (monitor pattern looks like 100x200?) so I can't mount it, (2) USB-C dock charges but USB peripherals (webcam + keyboard) connected to it behave flaky (camera flickers/on-off), and (3) trying to join corp-secure Wi-Fi I get a popup saying '802.1X: no certificate available' after SSO. Who's best to ping?

Marco - Facilities: Welcome Izzy! :wave: We sometimes get monitors with an odd vertical VESA pattern. If you can send a photo of the mount holes I can check if we have a drop-in adapter (75x75 <-> 100x200). I can drop a temporary stand/desk clamp today if you need immediate setup.

Izzy Wong: Thanks Marco 60a Photo attached in DM. The pattern is two vertical holes spaced 100mm apart and two more at 200mm vertical total. Desk is E-9 so a temporary stand works for now.

Devin (IT): Hey Izzy, sorry for the hiccups. For the dock: can you confirm OS? Also please try direct-attach the webcam to laptop to confirm the camera itself is stable. If direct-attach is fine, we likely have a dock firmware/USB muxing bug.

Izzy Wong: On macOS Sonoma image. Directly plugged webcam is stable. When webcam is on dock the video feed shows for ~10s then goes black, reconnect sound plays. Keyboard sometimes misses keystrokes too.

Devin (IT): Thanks. I've opened ticket IT-370777 and added you as reporter. Quick triage while we queue fixes: 1) In Terminal run `system_profiler SPUSBDataType` and paste the block for the dock; 2) In Console.app filter for USB or IOUSBHost logs when it disconnects; 3) Does `ifconfig -a` show the dock Ethernet as en5 or similar and show an IP?

Izzy Wong: Pasting minimal outputs:
```bash
$ system_profiler SPUSBDataType | grep -A3 -i "DockModel"
DockModel: VServe-XL
Product ID: 0x2a10
Vendor ID: 0x1d6b (Linux Foundation)
```
And `ifconfig` shows `en5: status: active inet 10.14.23.45 netmask 0xffffff00` but upload speeds look very slow (zoom becomes choppy).

Devin (IT): Good data, thanks. Slow uplink + USB flapping suggests the dock's internal switch is renegotiating power or the hub firmware is faulty. Two action items: I'll schedule a vendor firmware push to the dock (IT-370777) at 17:30 PT and pre-stage a replacement dock if push fails. Also I'll enable a 45-minute VPN token so you can join calls if it drops during the push.

Liu (Shipping): Izzy 4e6 I flagged the VESA adapter (100x200 -> 75x75) and a spare USB-C dock for same-floor swap under IT-370777. ETA parts: VESA adapter today end-of-day, spare dock tomorrow morning. Tracking posted in the ticket when available.

supply-bot: [IT-370777] Parts requested: VESA adapter 100x200->75x75, spare USB-C dock. Firmware push scheduled 17:30 PT.

Marco - Facilities: I can drop a temporary stand at E-9 in ~20 min so you can mount the monitor and finish orientation. Want me to do that?

Izzy Wong: Please yes that would be amazing, orientation is in 40.

Devin (IT): VPN token DM'ed (45 min). Also for the 802.1X certificate error: on mac go to Keychain Access and search for any entries with the corp wifi hostname or 'edu-802.1x' and delete them. Then System Settings -> Network -> Wi-Fi -> Advanced -> 802.1X -> remove any saved profiles for corp-secure, reboot and rejoin. If that still says 'no certificate available' reply and I'll push a temporary profile.

Izzy Wong: Did the Keychain cleanup and rebooted, rejoin still fails but now the error says 'Server certificate not trusted'.

Devin (IT): That means the machine didn't receive the internal CA. I'm pushing a temporary profile to you now under IT-370777; accept the prompt and it should provision the CA cert. If it errors, ping here and I'll generate a manual profile.

supply-bot: [IT-370777] Update: Firmware push queued. VESA adapter and spare dock ordered. Network profile push in progress.

Marco - Facilities: Dropped temporary stand at E-9 and left a note. If you prefer a manual mount later, tag me and I'll book a time.

Izzy Wong: Stand in place, thank you Marco. Network profile prompt popped, accepted and joined corp-secure successfully. Also Devin the VPN token helped during the flakiness earlier, Zoom is stable for now.

Devin (IT): Great news. I'll monitor IT-370777 for the firmware push result and follow up whether we need a dock swap. Izzy, if camera or keyboard flake again, paste Console logs to the ticket and tag me.

Liu (Shipping): Tracking posted to ticket: VESA adapter delivery EOD, spare dock scheduled AM delivery.

Izzy Wong: All good so far 44d thanks everyone for the quick response!

Devin (IT): Closing loop for now: IT-370777 will track firmware push, spare dock allocation, and VESA adapter. Tag me if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
